title: Audit log storyboard for CISO briefing
content:
Purpose:
This is a concise briefing doc to arm GTM reps and solution engineers for CISO-level conversations focused on audit logging, telemetry guarantees, and data handling commitments for regulated buyers (healthcare, finance, public sector). Use as a slide storyboard + talking points.

Audience and context:
- Primary: CISOs, security architects, compliance leads evaluating Redwood for inference in production.
- Secondary: procurement/security review committees.
- Typical situation: customer has complex audit requirements and wants explicit wording they can copy into questionnaires or contract exhibits.

Top-line positioning (one-liner):
- "Redwood provides tamper-evident, query-level audit telemetry and contextual access logs that map directly to SOC2 and HIPAA evidentiary needs — with exportable, time-series audit streams for third-party review and retention policies you control."

Key proof points to surface quickly:
1) What we capture: request metadata (timestamp, model, model version, route), caller identity (API key, service account), IP/region, request/response size and token usage, sampling of prompt hashes (configurable), policy decision logs (routing/fallback events), and system events (deployments, model rollouts).
2) Tamper evidence & integrity: append-only, signed log export available for dedicated/private customers; cryptographic hash chain option for high-assurance engagements.
3) Retention & access control: configurable retention windows per workspace, role-based access for audit exports, integration with customer KMS for on-prem/private retention.
4) Queryability & exports: S3/HTTPS export hooks, SIEM connectors (Splunk/CrowdStrike/Datadog), and live audit stream via secure webhook for real-time monitoring.
5) Alignment to standards: mapping to SOC2 TG and CC controls and HIPAA audit requirements — we provide a one-page mapping artifact and sample contract language.

Sample CISO talking points (short):
- "We ship comprehensive, request-level telemetry out of the box and can shape exports to match your SOC2 audit evidence and HIPAA log retention policies."
- "For Dedicated and Private customers we can enable signed, append-only exports so you can validate log integrity during forensic reviews."
- "Retention and redaction are policy-controlled by you. We provide UI and APIs to manage retention windows and scrub PII before logs are exported."

Competitive differentiators to call out (how to frame vs. major competitors):
- Versus large cloud providers: We present inference-specific telemetry (model variants, token-level usage, KV-cache hits) rather than generic API logs — gives auditors direct traceability from request to model decision.
- Versus smaller hosters/self-hosted runtimes: We combine production-grade telemetry with operational playbooks and managed export integrations, reducing customer lift for audit readiness.
- Versus other API-first LLM providers: Our log schema includes model rollout identifiers and fallback events (helpful in incident reconstruction) and we publish a mapping to SOC2/HIPAA artifacts.

Recommended audit-log language snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- "Provider shall maintain per-request audit telemetry including timestamp, request identifier, serving model and model version, caller identity, request and response token counts, and any routing/fallback decisions. Provider shall make audit exports available in standard formats (JSON/NDJSON) and provide secure export hooks to customer-designated storage."
- "For Dedicated and Private deployments, Provider will offer cryptographically-signed append-only audit exports upon customer request to support evidence integrity checks during third-party audits."

Data handling and PII controls (talking track and example wording):
- Capture and redaction: default telemetry includes non-content metadata; full prompt/response capture is configurable and can be redacted or hashed prior to export per customer policy.
- Customer-managed keys: integrate with customer KMS where required so exported logs are encrypted under customer keys.
- Data residency: export endpoints can be scoped to region and storage targets to satisfy data residency controls.

Common CISO questions and scripted answers:
Q: "Do logs include full prompt text?"
A: "By default we capture metadata and configurable prompt hashes. Full prompt/response capture is available but is disabled by default and must be enabled per workspace with documented retention and redaction controls."

Q: "How do you prevent log tampering?"
A: "We provide append-only export options with cryptographic signing for Dedicated and Private customers. For Hosted customers we maintain standard immutability controls and can stream to customer SIEM for independent retention."

Q: "Can we get SOC2/HIPAA-specific mapping artifacts?"
A: "Yes — we maintain a one-page mapping artifact that ties each audit artifact to Redwood features and configuration steps (we'll attach during RFP responses)."

Operational checklist for SEs during an evaluation call:
- Confirm deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private and note any KMS or residency requirements.
- Ask about required retention period, export cadence, and SIEM connectors.
- Offer a short demo of the audit export flow (show NDJSON sample, filtering by workspace and time range).
- If customer requires signed exports, flag as engineering gating item and open a POC ticket.

Artifacts to attach to a proposal or RFP response:
- One-page SOC2/HIPAA mapping (artifact-to-control matrix).
- Sample NDJSON audit export (redacted).
- Access control RBAC guide for audit exports.
- Contract exhibit language for log export & integrity.

Open questions / engineering notes:
- Feasibility and timeline for on-demand signed export in Hosted tier (currently Dedicated/Private only).
- Option to support configurable hashing strategies for prompt redaction (SHA-256 vs salted HMAC) — track design as RFC.

Next steps for the GTM team:
- Iterate this storyboard into a short 2–3 slide CISO briefing for the enablement deck.
- Coordinate with security/product to produce the sample artifacts listed above.
- Add a template POC Jira flow for signed export requests to standardize delivery SLA.

Notes to self (draft tone, for internal iter):
- Keep wording explicit and non-technical during initial CISO call; escalate to SE with artifact handoff.
- Avoid absolute promises for Hosted tier until product-team confirms signed export roadmap.

End of doc.
